title: Do YOU need DesignaKnit
author: Sue Jalowiec
excerpt: DesignaKnit is a powerful tool for planning garment shapes, creating stitch patterns, and knitting with on-screen guidance — but it’s not a must-have for every machine knitter. Here’s a clear look at what DAK does, where it shines, and how to decide if it belongs in your knitting workflow.
metaTitle: Do You Need DesignaKnit? A Clear Guide for Machine Knitters
metaDescription: Wondering if DesignaKnit is worth it? Explore what DAK does, how it fits manual, punchcard, and electronic machines, and whether it belongs in your knitting toolkit.
body:
Do You Need DesignaKnit?

Short answer: no.
Better answer: maybe — if the way you like to knit matches what DAK does best.

Let’s walk through what DesignaKnit can do, how it fits different types of machines, and some ways to decide whether it’s worth your time and money.

What Is DesignaKnit, Really?

DesignaKnit (DAK) is knitting software that helps you:

  • Shape garments on screen
  • Create and manage stitch patterns
  • Get row-by-row instructions for your projects

It’s popular with machine knitters who have electronic machines, but you don’t need an electronic machine to get value from it. Many knitters use DAK with:

  • Manual machines (like the LK150)
  • Punchcard machines
  • Hand knitting projects

Think of DAK as a very smart pattern and charting assistant. You can do everything it does by hand — it just helps you do it faster, more accurately, and with more “undo” options.

What Does DesignaKnit Actually Do?

1. Creates Garment Patterns

In the Shape side of DAK, you can:

  • Choose from a library of hundreds of basic garment styles
  • Adjust measurements and shaping to match your ideas
  • Print instructions in different formats:
    • Row-by-row written instructions
    • Japanese notation
    • Interactive Knitting (on-screen prompts)

This is especially helpful if you:

  • Want to tweak sizing confidently
  • Re-use a favorite silhouette
  • Prefer your patterns tidy and consistent

Without DAK, you can still:

  • Use ready-made patterns (like those at Knit by Machine)
  • Convert hand-knitting patterns
  • Use vintage machine patterns
  • Draft shapes manually

2. Creates Stitch Patterns

On the stitch pattern side, DAK lets you:

  • Build stitch patterns visually
  • Download patterns to many electronic machines
  • Print punchcard diagrams
  • Print charts for manual or hand manipulation

Without DAK:

  • Use built-in patterns in your machine
  • Manually program stitches
  • Use pre-punched cards
  • Punch your own from books or vintage resources
  • Hand-manipulate stitches from a chart

3. Interactive Knitting and Extras

DAK also includes “bonus” tools:

  • Interactive Knitting — step-by-step on-screen prompts for shaping, color changes, and stitch patterning
  • Graphics tools — import images, trace shapes, build custom color charts

Do You Need DesignaKnit?

You’ll probably get a lot of value from DAK if:

  • You design or tweak garments often
  • You want consistent, repeatable sizing
  • You love experimenting with stitch patterns
  • You want to knit from on-screen prompts
  • You’re willing to learn new tools

You might wait or skip DAK if:

  • You mostly follow ready-made patterns
  • You’re still building basic machine-knitting skills
  • Tech drains your energy
  • You’re not sure yet what you enjoy knitting

DAK is a large program with a learning curve. If you’ll use its big features often, it can absolutely earn its place in your toolkit. If not, your budget might be better spent on yarn, patterns, or a workshop.

What If You Have a Manual or Punchcard Machine?

Good news: DAK is not just for electronic machines.

With a manual or punchcard machine, you can use DAK to:

  • Plan garment shapes
  • Print charts for stitch patterns
  • Print punchcard layouts
  • Use Interactive Knitting as a row-by-row chart

But I’m Overwhelmed by Tech…

Many knitters feel this way at first. You don’t have to use everything. You can:

  • Start with one small goal
  • Ignore the menus you don’t need yet
  • Add features as you go

Take it step by step. You don’t have to master the whole program to get meaningful value.

Using DAK Alongside Knit by Machine

Knit by Machine supports you with or without DAK. You can use:

  • Tools, patterns, Skill Builders, and Smart Guides on their own
  • Or combine them with DAK for deeper design control

DAK is one way to streamline your knitting — not the only way.

Want a Closer Look at DAK?

LearnDesignaKnit.com/QUICK

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need DesignaKnit to use my knitting machine?

No. Your machine works perfectly on its own. DAK simply adds planning and visualization tools.

Will DAK work with my manual or punchcard machine?

Yes. You can still plan shapes, print charts, and follow instructions manually.

What is Interactive Knitting?

A feature that walks you through each row. For some electronic setups, it can also track carriage direction and shaping steps automatically.

I’m not “techy.” Is DAK too hard for me?

You don’t need to use every feature. Start small, follow step-by-step guidance, and build confidence one piece at a time.
